set.body:
Journey: Share, and Open. Track: engine.

Outcome
Anyone permitted to read a release, or a shared subset, downloads it as one archive and can verify it. An operator can do the same from the command line.

Why
Over HTTP a release can be downloaded only one file at a time. Whole-release export exists only as a developer call.

Acceptance
1. An export route streams a tar or zip of one fixed release or accepted view, with directories preserved, without holding the release in memory.
2. The archive contains a checksum manifest at a fixed name, listing path, size and SHA-256. A documented one-line command verifies it.
3. Access is checked during the stream, as it is for single files. A download that is revoked or cancelled does not end as a valid archive.
4. The operator command exports the same release to a directory. This exists as a developer call and needs exposing.
5. Throughput is measured on a release of at least 5 GiB that includes a file over 1 GiB. Authority is rechecked every 64 KiB today, and the 18 November audit reads the code as reloading the installation's policy on each check. If the rate is under 20 MB per second on the pilot host, bring forward the scoped authority read (OPS02) for the delivery path, keeping revocation in mid-stream.

Not in scope
The transfer manifest for exchange between installations (INT02, parked). Resumable downloads. Public links.

Start from
- modules/objects/src/main/scala/sanctity/objects/DirectoryExport.scala.
- modules/application/src/main/scala/sanctity/application/NativeRepository.scala line 122: delivery and its authority checks.
- modules/http/src/main/scala/sanctity/http/RepositoryHttp.scala line 182: the single-file route.

Evidence
An integration test that compares the HTTP and command-line output with the release inventory. The Share step of CORE1. The measured rate goes to CORE3.
